chapter_theme: A song at Yazhppanayanpattinam (யாழ்ப்பாணாயன்பட்டினம், Jaffna): the poet asks to be rid of desire for women whose eyes are Kama's arrows and Death's messengers and who bind the rich with illusion, and to gain knowledge by Murugan's word; the praise is a litany of the goddess and Murugan as guru and giver of Tamil.

759.reading: The poet describes flower-haired women whose glance is spear and sword, Kama's war arrows and Death's own messenger, who daily bind those with money in hand in delusion, skilled in illusion, with nectar lips and lying words, thread waists and perfumed, jewelled breasts, and asks Murugan to destroy his desire for their bodies and grant that by his true word he gain knowledge and worship him. The praise is a litany of the mother: Vishnu's sister, the maiden Uma, Sivai who dances in bliss, Tripurai, Bhairavi among ghouls, lady of the worlds who makes, holds and destroys and dwells at Siva's side in play; her son is the guru of the renouncers' knowledge and the giver of the Tamil prosodists weigh, at Yazhppanayanpattinam with its golden walls.
759.nuance: நமன் விடு தூது: the women's eyes are Death's messengers, joining the book's two themes in one image. கைப்பொருள் உடையவர் marks them as women who want money. The goddess litany (திரிபுரை, பயிரவி, புவநேசை) uses Sakta names. யாழ்ப்பாணாயன் பட்டினம் is Jaffna, one of the book's shrines in Lanka.

source_issues: Heading: யாழ்ப்பாணாயன்பட்டினம் is Jaffna (யாழ்ப்பாணம்); the song's last line has the same form.
